--apply would run these 7 steps against the cluster your kubeconfig names, in order, stopping at the first failure:

1. Check that helm runs and release maul is installed in namespace maul
     helm version --short
     helm status maul -n maul

2. Apply the relay's Dex client secret in namespace maul
     kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts --field-manager=maul-setup-previews -f maul-previews/secrets/maul-preview-auth-dex.secret.yaml

3. Apply Dex's copy of the client secret in namespace dex (skipped when no such namespace is here: Dex runs elsewhere)
     kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts --field-manager=maul-setup-previews -f maul-previews/secrets/dex-maul-preview-auth-client.secret.yaml

4. Apply the Certificate preview-wildcard in namespace maul
     kubectl apply --server-side --force-conflicts --field-manager=maul-setup-previews -f maul-previews/manifests/certificate.yaml

5. Wait for certificate/preview-wildcard to be Ready
     kubectl -n maul wait certificate/preview-wildcard --for=condition=Ready --timeout=10m0s

6. Upgrade release maul to chart 0.12.41 with your values, then maul-previews.values.yaml
     helm upgrade maul oci://ghcr.io/devthenet-labs/maul/charts/maul --version 0.12.41 -n maul -f values/maul.yaml -f maul-previews/maul-previews.values.yaml --wait --timeout 10m0s

7. Run the checks of maul check previews
     maul check previews -n maul

Manifests are server-side applied as maul-setup-previews; a Secret's contents are never printed.

Left to you after it, as NEXT-STEPS.md says:
  - preview nodes, labelled and tainted (NEXT-STEPS.md step 2)
  - preview image pulls on those nodes (step 3)
  - Dex: its static client maul-preview-auth and the secret's environment variable, then roll Dex (step 4)
  - the two DNS records (step 7)
